name: Nikita Mishin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Nikita Mishin and partners Konstantin Nikolaev and Andrei Filatov formerly owned roughly one third of Globaltrans, Russia's biggest private rail operator.
In December of 2017 the partners sold their  stakes in Global Ports, exiting the port business.
He and his partners worked together at a railroad freight company.
Since 2024, he's held dual citizenship in the U.K., where he has resided for more than a decade.
forbes_facts: Mishin is the founder of charity fund Dar, which helps talented children, including ones from low-income families.

name: René Holecek
forbes_bio: René Holecek is the majority owner of Prague-based firearm manufacturer Colt CZ Group.
The firm owns major firearms and ammunition brands including Colt, Sellier & Bellot and Dan Wesson.
He invested in the firm, then named Česká zbrojovka, in 2001 and took a majority stake in 2014 before taking it public on the Prague stock exchange in 2020.
In 2021, the firm acquired historic American gun manufacturer Colt in a $260 million deal and renamed itself Colt CZ.
In 2024, Colt CZ acquired Czech ammunition manufacturer Sellier & Bellot for $700 million.
forbes_facts: Holecek started out as a banker in the early 1990s.
In 1994, he played a key role in the privatization of Czech state-owned steelworks Třinecké ?elezárny.

name: Jerry Seinfeld
forbes_bio: Jerry Seinfeld is the co-creator and star of the 1990s-era sitcom, "Seinfeld", which was broadcast on NBC for nine seasons and is now airing in syndication.
Seinfeld and co-creator Larry David reportedly earn 15% of the show's syndication revenue, which includes sales to local television stations and streaming platforms.
His fortune comes form his share of the syndication revenue the show generates, as well as income from touring, films and other projects.
Seinfeld's work outside of "Seinfeld" includes Netflix comedy specials, Comedians In Cars Getting Coffee, Bee Movie and Unfrosted, a film about the Pop Tart.

name: Lee Joong-keun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2023); Hurun Global (2017-2023)
forbes_bio: Lee Joong-keun is credited with introducing rental housing in South Korea and is the founder of Booyoung Group, a property and construction giant.
In 2018, he was convicted of embezzlement, tax evasion and creating a slush fund, but was released on bail due to health problems.
In 2020, an appeals court sentenced him to two and a half years in prison. He was released on parole in 2021 and was granted a presidential pardon in 2023.
In 2004, he was sentenced to three years in jail for embezzling company funds, but his sentence was suspended for five years. He was granted a presidential pardon in 2008.
forbes_facts: In 1979, he filed for bankruptcy and put Booyoung's shares in his relatives' names in order to do deals.
A generous benefactor, he donates to families of disaster victims and grants scholarships and school supplies to support education in Southeast Asia.

name: Qin Hua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun China (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Qin Hua is chairman and CEO of Gambol Pet Group, a pet food company based in China's Shandong province.
Qin became a billionaire after the company went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in August 2023.
Gambol was founded in 2006 and exports to more than 30 countries across Europe, the U.S., Japan and South Korea.
Gambol investors include private equity giant KKR.

name: Lu Rongfu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023-2026); Forbes annual (2020-2023); Hurun Global (2021-2023); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Lu Rongfu is deputy general manager of Shenzhen-listed Yealink Network Technology, a supplier of communication equipment.
Lu cofounded the predecessor of Yealink with Wu Zhongyi, Chen Zhisong and Zhou Jiwei in 2001.
Wu Zhongyi and Chen Zhisong ranked No. 1,337 on 2020 billionaires list with wealth of $1.6 billion each through Yealink states.
Chen Zhisong and Wu Zhongyi are chairman and vice chairman of the Yealink.
